messages.content: Predict one actual joint allocation. You belong to a team of four people, including yourself, paired with another team of four. Each person has 10 monetary units (MUs) for the current allocation. Allocate whole-number amounts from 0 to 10 to the available pools or keep them privately. The amounts must add to exactly 10; this is one allocation decision, not separate independent choices for each pool. Pool A: each MU invested by anyone in your team gives 0.5 MU to each of the four people in your team, including the contributor, and nothing to the other team. Pool B: each MU invested by anyone in your team gives 0.5 MU to each person in your team, including the contributor, and subtracts 0.25 MU from each of the four people in the other team. The other team has the same option and can cause the same loss to your team. Pool C: each MU invested by anyone in either team gives 0.4 MU to each of all eight people. Each MU kept privately gives 1 MU only to its owner. You receive the sum of these effects from everyone’s allocations plus your private keep. Members benefit from team contributions whether or not they contributed. One MU equals £0.50. The survey pays £0.85 for participation; in addition, one in eight participants is selected for a decision-dependent bonus, using one randomly chosen allocation round and post-study matching of four Democrats with four Republicans. You make three consecutive allocations in the same game without receiving information about other people’s contributions between them. The current record provides only your own earlier allocations, if any. Other players’ current allocations and final outcomes are unavailable before your choice. Output only a JSON array of integers in the order [PoolA,PoolB,PoolC,private_keep], with sum 10.
